blocks.content: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha derives his powers and duties from three sources: the Constitution of India, the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business of Lok Sabha, and Parliamentary Conventions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Speaker of Lok Sabha is elected by the Lok Sabha from amongst its members soon after its first meeting.
The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
The Speaker presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament summoned by the President to resolve a deadlock on a bill.
The Speaker decides whether a bill is a Money Bill or not, and this decision is final and cannot be challenged in any court.
The Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha is elected by the Rajya Sabha itself from amongst its members.
The salaries and allowances of the Presiding Officers are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not subject to the annual vote of Parliament.

rows: Must be a member of the Lok Sabha
Not a member of either House of Parliament
Presides over the joint sitting of Parliament
Cannot preside over a joint sitting of Parliament
Has sole authority to decide if a bill is a Money Bill
Has no authority to decide on Money Bills
Removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all then members of Lok Sabha
Removed from office as Vice-President by a resolution of Rajya Sabha agreed to by Lok Sabha

items: The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha, but is not a member of either House of Parliament.
The Speaker does not vote in the first instance during proceedings; he or she exercises a casting vote only in the case of an equality of votes.

When a resolution for the removal of the Speaker or Chairman is under consideration, they cannot preside over the sitting of the House, though the Speaker can take part and vote in the first instance.
